steps.text: Quartiere Saluzzo

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Leon.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: I've never been one to tell you what to do. I've always hoped you'd come to your own decisions about everything.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: You've done well, all these years.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: If you really think that, then why...
Why did you suddenly decide to act now?
Why are you telling me this?
Why... did you betray Lavinia?
Countless questions swirl around Leontuzzo's mind, but none of them leave his lips.
What he just saw and heard seems to contradict his cognition. He suddenly feels as if the man before him is not his father. He's like a stranger.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Because this is the best, and only chance.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: What do you mean by that?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: You'll find out soon enough.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Signor Bernardo, Signor Leontuzzo, it's a pleasure to see you.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Hmm? You're not one of Saluzzo's associates.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Segretario di Sicurezza Alimentare, Rubio. Why are you...?

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: My dipartimento is catering tonight's banquet. I'll be cooking, personally.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: I've heard that in Volsinii, no event worth its salt can be held without the endorsement of il Dipartimento di Sicurezza Alimentare.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: You speak too highly of me.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: I'm just hoping to make food that satisfies the fine men and women of every famiglia.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Yet another reason to look forward to tonight's banquet.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: You came.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Where is he right now?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: He went to the Saluzzo mansion.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Okay.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: You're not going to ask why?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I can tell that Bernardo is very important to you.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: When I became a judge, he didn't ask me to abuse my position to protect the famiglia backing me, like all the other judges.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: He let me do what I wanted to do.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Leon, too.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: As the Bellone boss in this city, he respects my work and the brand of justice I seek to uphold.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Even if I rule against the Bellones, he sees it as strictly business.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: In his words, my justice is more effective than blind violence.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I don't object to his understanding of justice. He even spends some of his spare time reading law literature.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Even so, as a judge, I still have to come face-to-face with the injustices that constantly plague this city.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: The power struggles between the famiglie, their oppression of the common folk, and the silent rage of the masses...

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: The more I tried to uphold justice, the more difficult I realized my path was.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I used to comfort myself that 'at least I'm not the tool of some famiglia.'

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: But how could that be true? My hands are already dirty.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I just didn't want to want to admit it. It's impossible not to get your hands dirty.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Even if this seems silly to you...

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: The promise Bernardo made to me was the only reason I was able to remain a judge in Siracusa.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Promise?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: He once told me that after Famiglia Bellone emerged victorious, he would carve out a piece of land in Siracusa.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: There, the law I placed my faith in would no longer rely on pure power, where the justice I sought could truly be realized.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: He's hoped I could be patient until that day comes.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Every time I start to think I can't bear it anymore, I think of his promise.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Tell me, if all of this was a lie, then what purpose has my life had for the past ten years?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I think... given his power and status, he wouldn't need to lie to you like that.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Right? That's why—

steps.name: Saluzzo Mafioso
steps.text: Who is it?

steps.name: Saluzzo Mafioso
steps.text: Huh? You're—

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I am Judge Lavinia. I would like to speak with Don Alberto regarding the murder of Carracci.

steps.name: Saluzzo Mafioso
steps.text: Your Honor... The Don is entertaining an honored guest right now and doesn't have time to...

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: By honored guest, do you mean Bernardo Bellone?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Please inform the two dons that this matter is of great importance.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I will not leave until I see them.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Please try this one. I learned it from a Leithanian chef.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Not bad, not bad.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Times have really changed, Bernardo.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: In the old days, whenever we wanted something, it was all: 'I must have it, and I'll kill anyone who gets in my way.'

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: But now?

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: I need to find officials or businessmen who are on good terms with me, and ask them to get it for me. Be discreet about it too. Wouldn't want news to get out.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Ridiculous.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Isn't that right, Rubio?

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Ah... Anything you desire, can be yours, Don Alberto. For one to be called upon to get what you want is his honor.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Hah.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Segretario Rubio, you must've been plenty lucky yourself to fill that position.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: I didn't have that kind of luck, which is why I had to go about it this way. I'm just a clown, currying favor with the bosses.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Heh. Look at this guy, always talking himself down. The fact that you're even here today is enough to prove your worth.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: You're right, Don Alberto.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Alright, Bernardo. We've spent enough time exchanging pleasantries, so let's get down to business.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: You want to do what the Dodici Famiglie have always wanted to do, but never had the guts—take her down.

spans.text: You want to do what the Dodici Famiglie have always wanted to do, but never had the guts—take

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: And sure. You have my support.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: But you've only just muddied the waters. If you really want to overthrow her, you're a long way away.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: The fact that you even dared to come to this dinner shows that the cards are still in your hand.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: So tell me, what exactly do you plan to do?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Alberto, what do you think about Famiglia Rossati?

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Rossati?

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: They've got ambition.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Famiglia Rossati isn't alive today just because Giovanna's standing up as Salvadore's successor.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Someone must think the legacy of the Texas name—old Salvadore's knack for unification, was an invaluable asset.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: If you ask me, it's a liability.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Charisma this, charisma that. In the end, money is what talks. It's the only thing that'll get anyone to give a damn about you.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: You're right. And also wrong.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: From where we stand, there are always methods of convincing people.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: And to be fair, I do somewhat admire Giovanna.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: While the Texas legacy did make for a liability, she took it up willingly, and managed to make it her own..

spans.text: make for a liability, she took it up willingly, and managed to make it her own..

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: It's true that the Rossatis have depended on the wealth and connections they've accumulated.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: But, they've gone too far.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: In what way?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Do you really think she wants to hand over the key to the new city to either of our famiglie?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: We've been jostling for power here, but the Rossatis haven't shown the slightest interest in participating, as if they're not even here in our world.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: But, they are the same Rossatis that took up Salvadore's legacy. They handed over the technology to build that city to Siracusa. Do you really think they're bystanders in all this?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: To a new city built to commemorate Salvadore?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: A new city that could change the trajectory of Siracusa?

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: You mind putting it in plain Siracusan for me?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: How could I possibly be more direct, Alberto?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: The Dodici Famiglie have been battling here in Volsinii. And to her, this is nothing more than a beast-fighting exhibition.

steps.name: Loyal Mafioso
steps.text: Don Alberto... (*whispers*)

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Hmm? Judge Lavinia, and Cellinia?

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: They want to see me and Bernardo?

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: What's the meaning of this, Bernardo?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: They're not with me.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: The Saluzzos have never been anything but hospitable to our guests.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: But, to those who are not guests—

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: You can deal with them according to the Saluzzo way.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Haha, alright then. You heard the man?

steps.name: Loyal Mafioso
steps.text: Yes, Don Alberto.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Bernardo, I know you enjoy chatting about plans, and the future.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: But I like more practical topics, myself.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Because you know those like the back of your hand.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: The people know the Saluzzos never place a bet lightly. But few remember that when a Saluzzo does place a bet, he doesn't let it go lightly either.

spans.text: The people know the Saluzzos never place a bet lightly. But few remember that when a Saluzzo
place a bet, he doesn't let it go lightly either.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Heh.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Rubio, the rest is not meant for your ears.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: I get it—

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Segretario Rubio, do you have any interest in opera?

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: Oh... I sometimes go, when I have the time.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Perfect.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Take this.

steps.name: Rubio
steps.text: This is... a ticket to 'La Morte di Texas' Act II?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Yes. If it sounds like something you'd be interested in, feel free to go check it out.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: I told you, Bernardo. The time for pleasantries is over.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: I'd also like to invite all Saluzzos and their associates to enjoy the show together.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: What are you talking about?

steps.name: Loyal Mafioso
steps.text: It's time to go.

steps.name: Loyal Mafioso
steps.text: This is a private party.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: And what if I told you I must see the dons today?

spans.text: And what if I told you I

steps.name: Loyal Mafioso
steps.text: The Saluzzos have a particular way of showing hospitality to unwelcome guests.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I'm sorry, Cellinia.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: This is what I'm here for, isn't it?

steps.name: Loyal Mafioso
steps.text: You dare pull your sword on a Saluzzo? Cellinia, last of the Texases, are you outta your mind?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Flip that one around.
To kill, not for the sake of killing, but for an honest and sincere hope—since her return to Siracusa, this is the fight that has felt the least empty to her.
That is what Texas thinks.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: My theater manager informed me that Famiglia Rossati has reserved a VIP box for tomorrow night's show.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Haha, staging a hit in a theater? Is that how the esteemed artistic director of Compagnia dell'alba operates?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: It's just sprinkling the dressing of truth onto a play.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: But, there is one thing I still have doubts about.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Giovanna has heavies from Columbia among her associates.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Especially her boss in this city, Wallach. I've heard rumors of his methods.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: How are you sure we'll be able to bring her down together?

steps.name: Radical Mafioso
steps.text: Don Alberto... (*whispers*)

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Haha, sounds like fun.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Bernardo, the judge and that Texas... very much want to see us.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: They've already wounded some of my soldiers.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: They are both close friends of yours, Bellone. Care to explain?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: The associates of Famiglia Saluzzo have always been known for their bloodlust and combativeness.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Alberto, if the Rossatis came to attack your home...

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: What do you think their chances would be?

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Zilch. They wouldn't stand a chance.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Cellinia will be the blade that runs through the heart of Famiglia Rossati.

steps.name: Alberto
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Where Rossati soldiers can't go, Cellinia can.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: So, what are you worried about? Can the Rossatis stop her?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I remember you.

steps.name: Loyal Mafioso
steps.text: I thought you totally gave up on this place, like you never even lived here.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: My time with the Saluzzos wasn't so bad.

steps.name: Loyal Mafioso
steps.text: Then, you gotta know what it is you're doing.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I do.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Texas, you...
Looking at the unconscious mafiosi strewn around her, Lavinia can't help but be briefly lost for words.
Even with all this, Texas was still holding back. She thought she had seen it all in her time dealing with the famiglie, but this is still beyond her comprehension.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I'm glad I'm on your side.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Unfortunately, it looks like this is as far as we'll get.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Leon?!

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Lavinia... you shouldn't have come.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I have to ask Bernardo something, face-to-face.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: The assassination of the boss of Famiglia Rossati has already been decided.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Saluzzo and Bellone will join forces.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: That's the decision they made?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: It was our decision.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Where is he?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Dinner just ended. My father is upstairs.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: You can see him, but nothing will change.
Along the way, Lavinia keeps running over a million different things to say.
There are too many questions she wants to ask Bernardo.
She imagines the countless arguments she'd have with him, as well as their outcomes.
She thinks she has mustered enough anger.
However, when she steps through the door, the scene she encounters shakes her to the core.
Bernardo sits upright in a luxurious chair.
In his hand rests a legal codex adorned with thorns.
The very same as the one she holds in her hands.
He lowers his head and rubs the tome lightly with his palms, as if completely unaware—of the thorns digging into his hands, of the bright blood trickling down.
Her chaotic thoughts all freeze in this moment.
In the end, thousands of words condense into one—

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: The game is over, Lavinia.
That sentence alone is already enough for her.
Only a few moments of silence pass, but she is already sapped of all her strength.
Lavinia turns to leave and does not look back, frightened of the tears about to roll from her eyes.
Bernardo remains in place, uttering not a single word as a few drops of his blood dye the floor.
